digest.component_or_area: CI/CD GitHub Actions dispatch and workflow scheduling
propositions: GitHub Actions runner pool saturates under Gerrit Verified dispatch bursts despite tickets-branch pushes producing zero workflow runs
Current per-run job cost ranges from 17 runner jobs (no mutation) to 24 runner jobs (all seven mutation shards), with immediate fan-out of 13 and peak theoretical demand of 19 concurrent jobs

Measured incident-period burst of seven runs in five minutes reached 22 waiting jobs and longest observed runner wait of 873 seconds; current-shape burst of three runs reached 22 waiting jobs with 197-second max wait, indicating repository-local and shared-org contention

Organization plan is Free tier with documented concurrency limit of 20 total and 5 macOS jobs; Actions API does not expose full organization-wide queue depth or billing, so measured repository queue is a lower bound

Four mutually exclusive first-move policy options have been costed: bundling preflights and capping mutation matrix to reduce immediate fan-out from 13 to 10 jobs (recommended), coalescing superseded patchsets with bounded savings, moving macOS to scheduled main health at coverage cost, or upgrading organization plan
